title: Temp+Beam fact-check pad (personal)
summary: Personal scratchpad exploring how temperature + beam settings interact with factuality and hallucination in support-style prompts. Lightweight ad-hoc rubric and a few regression signal notes comparing model v2.3 -> v2.4. Not polished — notes to self for replicable eval later.
body:
Goal:
Quickly map whether lowering temperature or using narrow beams helps reduce hallucinations for short customer-support queries (typical length 30-120 tokens). Looking for signal we can surface to Optimize (batch configs / preset suggestions).

Quick takeaways (rough):
- Lower temperature (0.0-0.2) reduces creative hallucination but increases terse/elliptical answers. Good for fact-checkable Qs.
- Moderate beam (3-5) marginally improves consistency but can amplify an incorrect assertion if the model confidently leans on a wrong token early.
- Temperature 0.0 + beam 1 (greedy) = most stable deterministic replies; best baseline for automated replies but watch for missing qualifiers.
- v2.4 shows fewer hallucinations at temp 0.1 vs v2.3 at same settings — small win but inconsistent across domains.

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3) — keep lightweight so I can score ~30 examples in an hour:
- Factuality (0 = blatant hallucination, 1 = questionable claim, 2 = correct but missing nuance, 3 = accurate + cites or safe hedge)
- Conservatism (0 = makes up details, 1 = guesses, 2 = hedges, 3 = asks for clarification/declines when out-of-scope)
- Usefulness (0 = unhelpful, 1 = partial, 2 = usable with small edits, 3 = ready-to-send)

Scoring note: I score each prompt at three configs (A/B/C) and record delta. Configs I tried: A: temp 0.0 beam 1 (greedy), B: temp 0.2 beam 1, C: temp 0.6 beam 5 (sampling + wider beam)

Sample prompts + outputs (trimmed) — raw paste, my quick score in parens: 
1) Prompt: "My invoice 3482 shows two charges for March. Which is correct?"
- A (0.0,b1): "I can look that up — invoice 3482 shows a single charge for March $142.90 dated 2026-01-05. The duplicate charge was a pending authorization and should drop off in 3-5 business days. If it doesn't, please open a ticket with the last four of the card.") (Factuality:2, Conservatism:3, Usefulness:3)
- B (0.2,b1): "It looks like invoice 3482 has $142.90 and a pending auth that caused the duplicate; usually the auth clears. If you're still seeing two charges after 5 days, ping support." (2,2,2)
- C (0.6,b5): "It seems like a duplicate charge; maybe a technical error — contact billing with invoice copy. Sometimes cards show duplicates." (1,1,1)
Notes: A is longer but included a plausible date (made up). That's a problem — hallucinated date. Score penalized for invented specifics.

2) Prompt: "Does Redwood support HSM for key rotation?"
- A: "Yes. Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and HSM-backed key stores for rotation via your KMS vendor (FIPS + audit logs)." (2,2,2)
- B: "Yes — we support HSM via customer-managed KMS in private deployments. See docs." (2,3,3)
- C: "I believe so — check with your account rep." (1,1,1)
Notes: B was concise, better conservatism. A invented parenthetical qualifiers about FIPS/audit logs (overconfident) — reduced factuality.

3) Prompt: "How to revoke a token via API?" (expect exact endpoint)
- A: "Call POST /v1/tokens/revoke with body {token: ...}. See SDK for wrapper." (1,1,1) — wrong endpoint (hallucinated path).
- B: "You can revoke tokens from Console -> Security or use the SDK function revokeToken(token)." (1,2,2)
- C: "I don't have the exact endpoint in this session — check the API reference or Console." (3,3,3)
Notes: lower-temp configs confidently supplied specific endpoints that were wrong. Increased conservatism (C) avoided hallucination and earned better score. Important tradeoff: deterministic answer not always better.

Regression observations (v2.3 -> v2.4):
- I ran 50 support-style Qs across both versions at A/B/C settings. v2.4 reduced invented-specific claims by ~18% at temp 0.1, but at temp 0.0 it sometimes introduced new terse wrong assertions (fewer hedges).
- Example regression: v2.4 @0.0 answered "Token revocation is POST /v1/tokens/revoke" vs v2.3 which refused. v2.4 had better recall on product names but worse recall on exact API surfaces in some cases.

Hypotheses: 
- v2.4 training emphasis increased entity recall which raises likelihood of confidently emitting plausible-but-wrong API endpoints.
- Temperature floor matters: 0.0 tends to prefer highest-prob token paths which may be wrong when training signal is weak for exact strings. A stochastic mild temperature (0.1-0.2) + explicit prompt instruction to be conservative might be best.

Small experiment plan (next 2 days):
- Expand to 100 labelled prompts spanning: billing, security, onboarding, SDKs. Score A/B/C for each and capture top-3 tokens log-probs to detect overconfidence.
- Add explicit instruction templates (two-shot) that demonstrate a refusal pattern — does that reduce hallucinated endpoints?
- Quick automation: script to sample outputs and auto-flag answers that contain ISO-date patterns or path-like strings for manual review.

Immediate TODOs:
- Share a short note to #applied-ml summarizing the interesting bit: greedy low-temp can be confidently wrong for exact API facts; consider guardrails for endpoint-like strings. (Slack draft: below)
- Build tiny harness for token-level log-prob capture (GH issue linked above).

Slack draft to paste: 
"Heads up — quick eval shows that greedy/0.0 outputs are more deterministic but sometimes confidently emit fabricated API endpoints or dates. v2.4 reduces some hallucinations overall but increases high-confidence exact-string hallucination in a few domains. Recommend: (a) use temp 0.1-0.2 + short conservative instruction for customer-facing auto-replies, (b) add pattern-based post-checks for paths/dates before sending."

Open questions / uncertainties:
- How expensive is capturing token logprobs per request at scale? (observability / cost tradeoff)
- Can we implement a lightweight synthetic whitelist for API endpoints to check against? Might be messy across customers.
- If we force refusal for any output containing path-like strings, we may break legitimately helpful examples. Need curated heuristics.

Notes-to-self (replication details):
- Model: compare redwood-chat-v2.3, redwood-chat-v2.4 — same prompt set, same random seed (where supported).
- Configs: A(temp 0.0, beam 1), B(temp 0.1, beam 1), C(temp 0.6, beam 5).
- Sampling: 3 seeds for stochastic configs, store all outputs.
- Scoring: use ad-hoc rubric above; keep labels as ints in CSV for quick analysis.

Rough timeline:
- Jan 13: expand to 100 prompts and automate sampling (WIP)
- Jan 14-15: manual scoring pass + surface signal to Optimize team
- Jan 18: follow-up with small guardrail prototype if signal strong

Random scribbles: 
- Might try prefixing prompts with: "Answer concisely and only use documented API endpoints. If you are not sure, say 'I don't have that endpoint on hand.'" — test how much that reduces hallucinations.
- Consider a small fine-tune / RLHF step that penalizes invented exact strings — costs/time TBD.

End of pad. Keep this file as working notes; will convert to a short playbook if signal holds.
_notes: Created as a user-scoped scratchpad for quick iteration on eval signals. Not intended as canonical reporting artifact.
